s: Who built the Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri?
x: The Panch Mahal, Buland Darwaza and Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri are Akbar's.

s: During which period did Fatehpur Sikri serve as Akbar's planned capital?
x: Fatehpur Sikri was Akbar's capital during 1571-1585 and shows Persian, Indian and Central Asian influences.

s: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of which Sufi saint, after whom Prince Salim was named?
x: Fatehpur Sikri was built in honour of Sheikh Salim Chishti, after whom Prince Salim was named.

s: Where does Shaikh Salim Chishti's white-marble tomb stand in a Jama Masjid courtyard?
x: Salim Chishti's white-marble tomb is in the Jama Masjid courtyard at Fatehpur Sikri.

s: Which styles does Jodha Bai's palace at Fatehpur Sikri combine?
o: Hindu trabeate and Islamic arcuate styles
European Gothic and Islamic arcuate styles
x: Jodha Bai's palace combines Hindu trabeate construction (beams and lintels) with Islamic arcuate construction (arches and domes).

s: For what is the Diwan-i-Khas at Fatehpur Sikri noted?
x: The Diwan-i-Khas at Fatehpur Sikri has a single central carved pillar.

s: Which arch did Fatehpur Sikri introduce, later used at Jahangir Mahal, Orchha?
x: Fatehpur Sikri introduced the Tudor (four-centred) arch, continued at Jahangir Mahal, Orchha.

s: Which building at Fatehpur Sikri served as a house of worship where scholars of different religions held philosophical debates?
x: The Ibadat Khana was the House of Worship used for philosophical debates among scholars of various religions.

s: Which of the following is NOT at Fatehpur Sikri?
x: Akbari Mahal is in Agra Fort, not at Fatehpur Sikri.

s: Which event did Akbar commemorate by building the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri?
x: The Buland Darwaza (c. 1575) marks Akbar's victory over Gujarat, not Jahangir's birth.

s: Which building at Fatehpur Sikri is known as the 'Gate of Magnificence'?
x: The Buland Darwaza, the southern entrance to the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri, is called the Gate of Magnificence.

s: How many storeys does the Panch Mahal at Fatehpur Sikri have?
x: The Panch Mahal is a five-storeyed pillared building; its ground floor has 84 pillars.

s: Who built the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque?
x: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque was built by Sher Shah Suri; Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal, Red Fort and Jama Masjid, Delhi.

s: Which of the following statements about the two Mughal structures named Moti Masjid is correct?
o: The Moti Masjid in the Red Fort was built by Aurangzeb, whereas the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort was built by Shah Jahan.
The Red Fort Moti Masjid was built by Shah Jahan, whereas the Agra Fort Moti Masjid was built by Aurangzeb.
Both Moti Masjids were built by Akbar in Agra Fort.
Both Moti Masjids were built by Aurangzeb in Delhi.
x: Aurangzeb built the Moti Masjid in the Red Fort, while Shah Jahan built the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort.

s: Who was the architect of Agra Fort?
x: Kasim Khan was the architect of Agra Fort, the earliest Akbari-style work.

s: Who built the Moti Masjid in Agra Fort?
x: The Agra Fort Moti Masjid is Shah Jahan's; Aurangzeb built the one in the Red Fort, Delhi.

s: In which year did Nadir Shah take the Peacock Throne from the Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort?
x: Nadir Shah took the Peacock Throne from the Diwan-i-Khas, the private audience hall, in 1739.

s: What was the Rang Mahal in the Red Fort?
o: The palace of the royal women
The hall housing the Peacock Throne
x: Rang Mahal was the palace of the royal women; Diwan-i-Am was the hall of public audience.

s: In which year did Akbar build Allahabad Fort?
x: Akbar built Allahabad Fort in 1583.

s: Who rebuilt Lahore Fort?
x: Lahore Fort was rebuilt by Akbar; the Red Fort was Shah Jahan's.

s: What is the shape of the plan of the Red Fort at Delhi?
x: The Red Fort has the shape of an irregular octagon.

s: What was the name of the new capital city founded by Shah Jahan at Delhi?
x: Shah Jahan built Shahjahanabad, with the Red Fort and Jama Masjid.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Sikandar Lodi's Tomb was built by his son.
Humayun's Tomb was built under the supervision of Haji Begum.
Akbar's Mausoleum was completed by Akbar.
Sher Shah Suri's Tomb was built for himself.
x: Option C is incorrect: Akbar began his tomb at Sikandra, but Jahangir completed it. Ibrahim Lodi built Sikandar Lodi's tomb, Haji Begum supervised Humayun's, and Sher Shah built his own.

s: At which place is Rabia Daurani's Tomb, also called Bibi ka Maqbara, located?
x: Bibi ka Maqbara, the tomb of Rabia-ud-Daurani, is at Aurangabad in Maharashtra and is often called the Taj of the Deccan.

s: During which period did Nur Jahan build the marble tomb of her father Itmad-ud-Daula at Agra?
x: The tomb of Itmad-ud-Daula (Mirza Ghiyas Beg) was built in 1622-1628.

s: How was Rabia-ud-Daurani, whose tomb is the Bibi ka Maqbara, related to Aurangzeb?
x: Rabia-ud-Daurani was Aurangzeb's wife; their son Azam Shah built the tomb for his mother.

s: Humayun's tomb was the first of which kind of tomb in the subcontinent?
o: Octagonal tomb set in a tank
Tomb built entirely of white marble
x: Humayun's tomb was the first garden tomb in the subcontinent. It used red sandstone with white marble inlay and had the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture.

s: Which monument marked the transition from the Lodi tradition to the Mughal architectural tradition under the Sur rulers?
x: Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram marks the Sur transition in the evolution of Indo-Islamic tomb architecture.

s: Which of the following is regarded as the last major imitation in the Mughal garden-tomb tradition?
x: Bibi ka Maqbara is regarded as the last major imitation in the Mughal garden-tomb tradition.

s: Who built Sikandar Lodi's tomb?
x: Ibrahim Lodi built Sikandar Lodi's tomb, which has an earlier double dome.

s: Who were the architects of Humayun's tomb?
o: Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and Sayyid Muhammad
Kasim Khan and Mirak Mirza Ghiyas
x: Humayun's tomb was designed by Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and his son Sayyid Muhammad.

s: Who was the architect of Bibi ka Maqbara?
x: Ata-ullah, son of Ustad Ahmad Lahori, designed Bibi ka Maqbara.

s: Who built the Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad?
x: Azam Shah, Aurangzeb's son, built the Bibi ka Maqbara in his father's reign as the tomb of his mother Rabia-ud-Daurani.

s: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
x: Sher Shah built his own tomb at Sasaram in Bihar, set in a tank; it marks the move from Lodi to Mughal style.

s: Which Mughal monument is known as the 'Baby Taj'?
x: Itimad-ud-Daula's tomb at Agra is called the Baby Taj; Bibi ka Maqbara is the Taj of the Deccan.

s: For whom was the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daula at Agra built?
x: It was built by Nur Jahan for her father Mirza Ghiyas Beg (Itimad-ud-Daula).

s: Which monument has the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture?
x: Humayun's tomb has the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture; Sikandar Lodi's tomb had an earlier double dome.

s: The design of the Taj Mahal was particularly inspired by which earlier Mughal monument?
x: Humayun's Tomb provided an important design ancestry for the Taj Mahal, particularly through the garden-tomb form and use of a double dome.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Taj Mahal is NOT correct?
o: It was built entirely of red sandstone.
It is associated with the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal.
It was built at Agra by Shah Jahan.
It represents a high point of pietra dura and symmetry.
x: The Taj Mahal is principally constructed of white marble, not entirely of red sandstone. It is the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal and is noted for pietra dura and symmetry.

s: Who is identified as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal?
x: Ustad Ahmad Lahori is identified as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal.

s: From where was the white marble used in the Taj Mahal mainly obtained?
x: The Taj Mahal's marble came from Makrana in Rajasthan. Sasaram is the site of Sher Shah's tomb, Fatehpur Sikri was built mainly of red sandstone, and Kollur is known for diamond mines (the Koh-i-Noor).

s: With which case are the Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) rulings on protection of the Taj Mahal associated?
x: The Supreme Court's Taj Trapezium Zone rulings, including those concerning industrial pollution, were associated with the M.C. Mehta case in 1996.

s: Which historians called the Taj Mahal a product of the Indo-Persian tradition?
x: Fergusson and Percy Brown saw the Taj as Indo-Persian; V.A. Smith saw European and Asiatic genius combined.

s: What mainly causes the 'marble cancer' threatening the Taj Mahal?
x: Marble cancer is caused by sulphur dioxide pollution.

s: Where does the Taj Mahal tomb stand in its charbagh?
x: The Taj tomb stands at the river end of its charbagh, not at the centre.

s: What was the original name of Mumtaz Mahal, for whom the Taj Mahal was built?
x: Mumtaz Mahal was Arjumand Banu Begum; Dilras Banu was Aurangzeb's wife and Mehr-un-Nissa was Nur Jahan.

s: In which year was the Taj Mahal inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: The Taj Mahal and Agra Fort became UNESCO sites in 1983.

s: In which year was the Taj Mahal declared one of the New Seven Wonders of the World?
x: The Taj Mahal was chosen among the New Seven Wonders in 2007.

s: Where is Jahangir buried?
x: Jahangir's tomb is at Shahdara, Lahore; Akbar's is at Sikandra and Aurangzeb's at Khuldabad.

s: Which of the following pairs (Tomb – Location) is correctly matched?
x: Akbar's mausoleum is at Sikandra. Humayun's Tomb is in Delhi, Jahangir's at Shahdara near Lahore, and Itmad-ud-Daula's at Agra.

s: Where is Babur's final tomb located?
x: Babur's tomb is at Bagh-e-Babur in Kabul, although he was first buried at Agra.

s: Where is Aurangzeb buried?
x: Aurangzeb lies in a simple grave at Khuldabad near Aurangabad.

s: To which place did Akbar give the name 'Bahistabad'?
x: Akbar named Sikandra, founded by Sikandar Lodi, Bahistabad; his tomb lies there.

s: Which Baluchi chief handed over Dara Shikoh to Aurangzeb?
x: Malik Jeevan handed Dara Shikoh over; he was killed in 1659.

s: Where is the Char Minar located?
x: The Char Minar is in Hyderabad.

s: Who built the Char Minar at Hyderabad?
x: Char Minar was built at Hyderabad in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Qutb Shahi dynasty. It is not a Mughal monument.

s: In which year did Akbar begin the Agra Fort?
x: Agra Fort was begun in 1565; Allahabad Fort was built in 1583.

s:
Arrange the following monuments in chronological order:
1. Char Minar
2. Agra Fort (begun)
3. Taj Mahal (begun)
4. Jama Masjid, Delhi (begun)
x: Agra Fort was begun in 1565, Char Minar built in 1591, the Taj begun in 1632 and Jama Masjid, Delhi in 1650.

s: Where is Ram Bagh, built by Babur, located?
x: Babur's Ram Bagh is at Agra, not Lahore.

s: Which of the following was NOT built during the reign of Akbar?
x: The Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by Shah Jahan (1650–56); the other three belong to Akbar's reign.

s: Which traditions did Mughal architecture mainly blend?
x: Mughal architecture blended Persian, Timurid and Indian architectural elements.

s: Which Mughal ruler's reign is called the 'Golden Age' of Mughal architecture?
x: Shah Jahan built in white marble and his reign is called the Golden Age of Mughal architecture.

s: In which material were the Mughal buildings of Akbar's reign mainly built?
x: Akbar built in red sandstone; Shah Jahan in white marble.

s: Who introduced the charbagh garden tradition in Mughal architecture?
x: Babur introduced the charbagh, or four-quartered garden, tradition; Ram Bagh at Agra is an example.

s: Where was pietra dura first used on a large scale in Mughal architecture?
x: Pietra dura began under Jahangir, appeared on a large scale at Itimad-ud-Daula and peaked at the Taj Mahal.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Humayun's tomb has the first full Persian double dome in Mughal architecture.
2. Sikandar Lodi's tomb had a double dome earlier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are true: Sikandar Lodi's tomb had an earlier double dome, and Humayun's tomb has the first full Persian double dome of the Mughals.

s: Which comparison between the architectural phases of Akbar and Shah Jahan is correct?
o: Akbar is associated mainly with red sandstone, whereas Shah Jahan is associated mainly with white marble.
Akbar is associated mainly with white marble, whereas Shah Jahan is associated mainly with red sandstone.
Both rulers used only white marble.
Both rulers used only red sandstone.
x: Akbar's phase is represented by red-sandstone structures such as Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri, while Shah Jahan's phase is dominated by white marble, as in the Taj Mahal.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pietra dura — inlay of semi-precious stones
Double dome — inner and outer shells
x: Jali refers to lattice work. Mirror-work chambers are associated with the Sheesh Mahal.

s: For what is the Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga noted?
x: Its fully covered courtyard sets it apart from the open-court pattern of Mughal mosques.

s: Where was the jali (lattice work) of the Mughal style seen in the first Mughal garden tomb?
x: Jali work is noted at Humayun's tomb, also the first Mughal tomb with a double dome.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Ram Bagh was built by Babur at Agra, not Lahore. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Shalimar Gardens at Lahore were built under which Mughal ruler?
x: The Shalimar Gardens at Lahore were built under Shah Jahan. The Shalimar Bagh at Srinagar is associated with Jahangir.

s: Who built the Shalimar Bagh at Srinagar?
x: Shalimar Bagh, Srinagar, was built by Jahangir; Shalimar Gardens, Lahore, by Shah Jahan.

s: Who built Nishat Bagh on the Dal Lake?
x: Nishat Bagh was built by Asaf Khan, Nur Jahan's brother.

s: Who laid out the Pinjore garden in Haryana?
x: Pinjore was laid out by Fidai Khan in Aurangzeb's reign.

s: Which is regarded as the first Mughal garden in India?
x: Babur's Ram Bagh at Agra is the first Mughal garden.

s: To which place did the Bahmani Kingdom shift its capital from Gulbarga?
x: The Bahmanis moved their capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.

s: Where did Shivaji make his capital?
x: Shivaji's capital was Raigad; Pune was the centre of Peshwa power.

s: Which city was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire, on the Tungabhadra?
x: Hampi on the Tungabhadra was the Vijayanagara capital; Gulbarga was a Bahmani capital.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Qutb Shahi tombs — onion domes on square bases in gardens
Golconda Fort — acoustic warning system and piped water
Charminar — Persian arches with Deccani stucco
x: Charminar is not a fully covered courtyard mosque; that feature is associated with the Bahmani Jama Masjid at Gulbarga. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which of the following is a Qutb Shahi monument rather than a Mughal one?
x: Golconda Fort is Qutb Shahi; the other three are listed UNESCO Mughal sites.

s: In which year was the Red Fort Complex inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Red Fort Complex: 2007; Agra Fort and Taj Mahal: 1983; Fatehpur Sikri: 1986; Humayun's Tomb: 1993.

s: In which year was Fatehpur Sikri inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Fatehpur Sikri was inscribed in 1986; Agra Fort and the Taj in 1983.

s: In which year did Humayun's Tomb become a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
x: Humayun's Tomb was inscribed in 1993; the Red Fort Complex in 2007.

s: What did the Char Minar, built in 1591, mark?
x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the Char Minar in 1591 to mark the end of a plague.

s: Which of the following pairs (Dynasty – Centre of power) is correctly matched?
x: The Chandelas ruled from the Khajuraho region. The Senas ruled from Nadia/Nabadwip, the Delhi Sultanate from Delhi and the Mughals from Agra, Delhi and other centres.

s: Who built the Gommateshwara statue?
x: Chamundaraya built the Gommateshwara statue.

s: Pattadakal is a centre of which architecture?
x: Pattadakal is Chalukyan; Mahabalipuram is Pallava.

s: To which architecture do the temples of Khajuraho belong?
x: Khajuraho is Chandela; Thanjavur is Chola and Mahabalipuram Pallava.

s: Which pair of Mughal monuments was inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1983?
o: Humayun's Tomb and Red Fort Complex
x: Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal were inscribed in 1983; Fatehpur Sikri in 1986, Humayun's Tomb in 1993, Red Fort in 2007.

s: Where are the Qutb Shahi tombs, with onion domes on square bases, located?
x: The Qutb Shahi tombs stand at Ibrahim Bagh, Hyderabad.

s: Who wrote the Muntakhab-ul-Lubab?
x: Khafi Khan wrote the Muntakhab-ul-Lubab; Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.

s: Who wrote the Alamgirnama?
x: Mirza Muhammad Kazim wrote the Alamgirnama; Lahori wrote the Padshahnama.

s: By what other name is Babur's autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi, known?
x: Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also called the Baburnama, is Babur's autobiography in Chagatai Turkish.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was written by Minhaj-us-Siraj, whereas Tabaqat-i-Akbari is by Nizamuddin Ahmad.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Babur authored the Baburnama or Tuzuk-i-Baburi.
x: Option A is incorrect: the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh was written by Abdul Qadir Badauni, a critic of Akbar; Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama. Jahangir, Gulbadan Begum and Babur are correctly matched.

s: Who wrote the Padshahnama, the history of Shah Jahan's reign?
x: The Padshahnama is by Abdul Hamid Lahori; the Akbarnama is by Abul Fazl and the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh by Badauni.

s: Who wrote the Humayun-nama, a history of Humayun?
x: The Humayun-nama was written by Gulbadan Begum.

s: In which language was Babur's autobiography, the Baburnama, written?
x: Babur wrote the Baburnama in Turki; Rahim later translated it into Persian.

s: Which of the following pairs (Work – Author) is correctly matched?
x: Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh; the Tabaqat-i-Akbari is by Nizamuddin Ahmad, the Alamgirnama by Kazim and the Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum.

s: Which work is associated with Abul Fazl's account of Akbar's administration and empire?
x: Ain-i-Akbari, the third part of Abul Fazl's Akbarnama, describes Akbar's administration and empire. Humayun Nama is by Gulbadan Begum, Alamgir Nama by Muhammad Kazim and Tarikh-i-Firishta by Firishta.

s: What is the name of the third volume of Abul Fazl's Akbarnama?
x: The Akbarnama has three volumes; the third volume is the Ain-i-Akbari, on Akbar's administration and empire.

s: Ishwardas Nagar wrote the Futuhat-i-Alamgiri on the reign of which Mughal emperor?
x: Futuhat-i-Alamgiri by Ishwardas Nagar is a history of Aurangzeb (Alamgir)'s reign.

s: Who among the following wrote the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri?
x: The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is the autobiography of Jahangir himself.

s: Who wrote the Nushkha-i-Dilkusha, a work of Aurangzeb's period?
x: Nushkha-i-Dilkusha was written by Bhim Sen in Aurangzeb's period.

s: Who translated Babur's memoir, the Baburnama, into Persian?
x: The Turki Baburnama was translated into Persian by Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana under Akbar.

s: Who wrote 'India at the Death of Akbar' (1920), an economic study?
x: W.H. Moreland wrote India at the Death of Akbar (1920) and From Akbar to Aurangzeb (1923).

s: Who wrote 'The Agrarian System of Mughal India, 1556-1707' (1963)?
x: The Agrarian System of Mughal India (1963) is by Irfan Habib of the Aligarh school.

s: François Bernier, author of 'Travels in the Mogul Empire', served which Mughal prince?
x: The French traveller Bernier served Dara Shikoh and wrote Travels in the Mogul Empire (1656-1668).

s: Which title did Akbar give to Tansen, one of his Navaratnas?
x: Tansen moved from Raja Ramchandra of Rewa's court to Akbar's and was honoured as 'Mian'.

s: Which Mughal emperor ended court music yet himself played the veena?
x: Aurangzeb ended court music, but Persian works on classical music were produced in his reign and he played the veena.

s: Which one of the following musical forms is correctly matched with its Mughal-era patronage?
o: Tappa — Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
x: Khayal flourished at the court of Muhammad Shah ‘Rangeela’, particularly through Sadarang and Adarang. Dhrupad was associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar, while Tappa was refined by Shori Miyan.

s: At whose court was Baiju Bawra a dhrupad singer?
o: Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
x: Baiju Bawra sang dhrupad at the court of Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior.

s: Baz Bahadur, the musician famed for his romance with Rupmati, was the last Sultan of which kingdom?
x: Baz Bahadur was the last Sultan of Malwa (1555-1562); he was defeated by Akbar's general Adham Khan.

s: From whom did Tansen receive the title 'Tansen'?
x: The title 'Tansen' came from Raja Vikramjit of Gwalior; Akbar gave him the title 'Mian'.

s: At whose court did the khayal composers Sadarang and Adarang flourish?
x: Khayal grew at the court of Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela', with Sadarang and Adarang as its composers.

s: Under whom did dhrupad begin at the court of Gwalior?
o: Raja Man Singh Tomar, before the Mughals
x: Dhrupad began with Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior (1486-1516), before the Mughals; khayal and tappa grew under Muhammad Shah.

s: What is 'Mal Gurjari', linked with Raja Man Singh Tomar?
o: A female singer at his court
x: Mal Gurjari is a raga invented by Raja Man Singh Tomar, not a person.

s: What was the original name of Tansen?
x: Tansen's original name was Ramtanu Pande; Swami Haridas was his teacher.

s: At whose court did Tansen serve before Akbar sent a firman for him?
o: Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior
x: Tansen was first at the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa (Bandhavgarh); Akbar then called him to his court.

s: Which style of Hindustani vocal music had its origin in Vedic chanting?
x: Dhrupad has its origin in Vedic chanting and began at Gwalior under Man Singh Tomar, before the Mughals.

s: Who among the following was the guru of Tansen?
x: Tansen of Gwalior was a disciple of Swami Haridas.

s:
Consider the following statements about Tansen:
1. He was a disciple of Swami Haridas.
2. His tomb is at Agra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Tansen was Swami Haridas's disciple; his tomb is at Gwalior, not Agra.

s: Which of the following ragas is credited to Tansen?
x: Mian ki Todi, Mian ki Malhar and Darbari Kanada are Tansen's ragas; Mal Gurjari was Man Singh Tomar's.

s: Who refined the Tappa style of music in the late 18th century?
x: Tappa grew at Muhammad Shah's court and was refined by Shori Miyan of Awadh in the late 18th century.

s: The sitar combines the Persian setar with which Indian instrument?
x: The sitar = Persian long-necked lute (setar) + Indian veena.

s: Ustad Mansur is particularly associated with which aspect of Mughal painting?
x: Ustad Mansur, a painter of Jahangir's court, was renowned for depicting flora and fauna.

s: Which Persian master did Humayun bring to India to lay the foundation of the Mughal school of painting?
x: Humayun brought Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad; Basawan was Akbar-era and Mansur of Jahangir's court.

s: The Dastan-i-Amir Hamza (Hamzanama), begun under Humayun, comprised about how many paintings?
x: The Hamzanama had about 1,400 paintings made by about 100 artists, supervised by Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basawan — Jahangir's specialist in flora and fauna
Ustad Mansur — Akbar's leading manuscript illustrator
x: Abdus Samad was a Persian master associated with Humayun and Akbar and was given the title Shirin Qalam. Ustad Mansur was associated with Jahangir and Basawan with Akbar.

s: To the atelier of which Mughal emperor did the painter Basawan belong?
x: Basawan belonged to Akbar's reign; Jahangir's painters included Manohar, Bishandas and Mansur.

s: Who was the Tabriz-born master who first led work on the Hamzanama?
x: Mir Sayyid Ali of Tabriz first led the Hamzanama; Abdus Samad (Shirin Qalam) later headed the atelier.

s: Manohar, a portrait painter of the Akbar-Jahangir period, was the son of whom?
x: Manohar was the son of Basawan, a leading master of Akbar's court.

s: The Tarikh-i-Alfi is a history of which of the following?
o: The first thousand years of Islam
x: Tarikh-i-Alfi covers Islam's first millennium; the Akbarnama is Abul Fazl's history of Akbar.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Hamzanama is associated with Humayun and Akbar.
Padshahnama is associated with Shah Jahan.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Padshahnama is the illustrated chronicle of Shah Jahan's reign, not Babur's. Hamzanama with Humayun and Akbar, and Tarikh-i-Alfi with Akbar, are right.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Razmnama – Akbar's Maktab Khana translation bureau
x: The Razmnama was produced by Akbar's Maktab Khana. The Hamzanama goes with Humayun, the Akbarnama with Akbar and Abul Fazl, and the Padshahnama with Shah Jahan.

s: What was the occupation of the father of Daswant, a leading painter of Akbar's atelier?
x: Daswant, who worked on the Razmnama, was the son of a potter.

s: The Hamzanama, the first Mughal illustrated manuscript, took about how many years to complete?
x: The Hamzanama took about 15 years, with about 100 artists and about 1,400 paintings.

s: Which title was given to the Persian master Abdus Samad?
x: Abdus Samad was Shirin Qalam; Zari Qalam was Muhammad Husain of Kashmir, Nadir-uz-Zaman Abul Hasan and Nadir-ul-Asr Mansur.

s: Which painter of Jahangir's court was a master of portraiture?
x: Bishandas was Jahangir's master of portraiture; Basawan and Daswant belonged to Akbar.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Lilavati was translated by Faizi. Maulana Shah Muhammad Shahabadi was associated with the translation of Rajatarangini.

s: Who translated the Atharvaveda into Persian under Akbar?
x: Haji Ibrahim Sirhindi translated the Atharvaveda; Badauni and Naqib Khan worked on the Razmnama.

s: Lilavati, translated into Persian during Akbar's reign, was originally a work on which subject?
x: Lilavati was Bhaskaracharya's mathematical work, translated into Persian by Faizi during Akbar's reign.

s: Who wrote the Ayar-i-Danish?
x: Abul Fazl wrote Ayar-i-Danish; Kashifi wrote Anwar-i-Suhaili and Nasrullah Shirazi Kalila-wa-Dimnah.

s: In which language is the Molla Ramayanam written?
x: Molla Ramayanam is a Telugu work, unlike the Persian Razmnama and Persian Ramayana of Akbar's time.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Nashurullah translated the Panchatantra into Kalila-wa-Dimnah.
Abul Fazl translated the Panchatantra into Ayar-i-Danish.
Nizamuddin Panipati translated the Panchatantra into Yogavasistha.
Mulla Husain Waaiz Kashifi translated the Panchatantra into Anwar-i-Suheli.
x: Option C is incorrect: Nizamuddin Panipati translated the Yogavasistha into Persian, not the Panchatantra. Nasrullah, Abul Fazl and Kashifi did make Panchatantra versions.

s: What was Akbar's translation department at Fatehpur Sikri called?
x: Maktab Khana was Akbar’s translation department at Fatehpur Sikri.

s: Who supervised Akbar's Translation Department, which rendered Sanskrit, Arabic, Turkish and Greek works into Persian?
x: Faizi headed Akbar's Translation Department.

s: Who made Kalila-wa-Dimnah, a Persian version of the Panchatantra?
x: Kalila-wa-Dimnah is by Nasrullah Munshi Shirazi; Kashifi wrote Anwar-i-Suhaili and Abul Fazl the Ayar-i-Danish.

s: Who translated Bhaskaracharya's mathematical work Lilavati into Persian?
x: Faizi, head of the Maktab Khana, translated Lilavati into Persian.

s: Who translated Kalhana's Rajatarangini into Persian?
x: The Persian Rajatarangini was made by Maulana Shah Muhammad Shahabadi.

s: Dara Shikoh was associated with which Sufi order?
x: Dara Shikoh followed the Qadiri order and was associated with Miyan Mir and Muhibullah Shah.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sirr-i-Akbar — Persian translation of the Upanishads
Majma-ul-Bahrain — Persian translation of the Ramayana
Razmnama — Persian translation of the Atharvaveda
Lilavati — Persian translation of the Rajatarangini
x: Sirr-i-Akbar, meaning ‘The Great Secret’, was Dara Shikoh’s Persian translation of the Upanishads.

s: What is the main theme of Majma-ul-Bahrain, written by Dara Shikoh?
o: development of Urdu in Mughal cantonments
common ground between Sufism and Vedanta
military campaigns of Shah Jahan in Central Asia
administrative systems of the Mughals and Safavids
x: Majma-ul-Bahrain, meaning ‘Mingling of the Two Oceans’, explores the common ground between Sufism and Vedanta.

s: Who made the Latin version of Dara Shikoh's Sirr-i-Akbar, which took the Upanishads to Europe?
x: Anquetil-Duperron's Latin version of the Sirr-i-Akbar carried the Upanishads to Europe.

s: Dara Shikoh's Sirr-i-Akbar (1657) is a Persian translation of about how many Upanishads?
x: The Sirr-i-Akbar (1657) translated about 52 Upanishads into Persian.

s: Dara Shikoh was linked with which Qadiri Sufi saint of Lahore?
x: Dara Shikoh, a Qadiri Sufi, was linked with Miyan Mir and Muhibullah Shah.

s: What was Akbar's painting atelier of more than 100 painters called?
x: The Tasvir Khana illustrated the Hamzanama, Tutinama, Akbarnama and Razmnama.

s: In whose reign was the halo or nimbus behind the emperor's head introduced in Mughal painting?
x: Jahangir's painters introduced the halo or nimbus behind the emperor's head, reflecting the period's refined and naturalistic style.

s:
Arrange these emphases of Mughal painting in chronological order:
1. Portraits, albums, flora, fauna and naturalism
2. Foundation through Persian masters
3. Formal court scenes, albums and floral borders
4. Illustrated manuscripts and a large painting atelier
x: Humayun (Persian masters), Akbar (illustrated manuscripts), Jahangir (naturalism), Shah Jahan (formal court scenes): 2-4-1-3.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Jahangir's period is regarded as the zenith or Golden Age of Mughal painting.
During Jahangir's period, painting shifted from albums towards only large manuscripts.
Jahangir patronised European and Persian arts.
Jahangir's painting included portraits, birds, flowers, animals and nature.
x: Option B is incorrect: under Jahangir painting moved away from large manuscripts towards albums and single portraits. His era is the golden age, he patronised European and Persian art, and nature studies flourished.

s: When Aurangzeb withdrew patronage, painters moved to Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and which other region?
x: Painters moved to Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and Bihar; Bengal is not part of this association.

s: Muted naturalistic colours, perspective and shading are features of which school of painting?
x: Mughal painting used muted naturalistic colours, perspective and shading; Rajput painting was vivid and decorative.

s:
Assertion (A): Mughal painting developed the use of portraiture and smaller distant objects for spatial depth.
Reason (R): European painting was introduced at the Mughal court through the Portuguese.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: European pictures reached Akbar's court through the Portuguese, and that influence brought portraiture and the use of smaller distant objects to show depth.

s: Through whom did European pictures first reach Akbar's court?
x: European pictures reached Akbar's court through the Portuguese, bringing portraiture and spatial depth into Mughal painting.

s: In which year did the first Jesuit mission from Goa reach Akbar's court?
x: The first Jesuit mission, led by Father Rudolf Acquaviva, reached Akbar's court in 1580.

s: Who led the first Jesuit mission to Akbar's court in 1580?
x: Father Rudolf Acquaviva led it, with Father Antonio Monserrate and Brother Francis Henriques.

s: Kavindracharya Saraswati is associated with which one of the following achievements?
o: Persuading Shah Jahan to remit the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Prayag
Writing the Persian translation of the Baburnama
x: Kavindracharya Saraswati obtained Shah Jahan's remission of the pilgrim tax at Banaras and Prayag and wrote Kavindra-kalpalata in Hindi.

s: In which language is Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas written?
x: Ramcharitmanas is an Awadhi devotional poem, not a Mughal court manuscript.

s: Who wrote the Sur Sagar?
x: Surdas wrote Sur Sagar; Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas and Rahim composed Hindi dohas.

s: To which Bundela court did the Hindi poet Keshavdas belong?
x: Keshavdas, author of the Ramchandrika and Rasikpriya, was a poet of the Bundela court of Orchha.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Pair A is wrong: Keshavdas of the Orchha court wrote Ramchandrika, Kavipriya, Rasikpriya and Ratan Bavani, not Ram Rasayan (the MPPSC 2025 trap). Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas, Surdas Sur Sagar and Kavindracharya Saraswati Kavindra-kalpalata.

s: Which Navaratna of Akbar is famous for his Hindi dohas?
x: Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana, a Navaratna of Akbar, wrote Hindi dohas.

s: Who was the first writer of Deccani poetry in Telangana?
x: Mulla Khiali was the first to write Deccani poetry in Telangana.

s: In the Sultanate period, which was the language of administration, diplomacy and high culture?
x: Persian replaced Sanskrit and Arabic in official and elite functions, while Hindavi grew in camps and bazaars.

s: With whom is the first Urdu poetic diwan associated?
x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is known for the first Urdu poetic diwan; Dakhni grew as a literary medium under the Qutb Shahis.

s: The translation movement, Persian-Indian painting and the development of Hindavi and Urdu together contributed to the growth of which cultural formation?
x: The interaction of translation, painting and Hindavi-Urdu literature helped create a composite Indo-Persian culture.

s: Under the Qutb Shahis, the official language was Persian. Which was the people's language?
x: The Qutb Shahi official language was Persian and the people's language Telugu.

s: Where did Urdu (Rekhta) mainly grow up in the Mughal period?
o: In the Sufi khanqahs of Bengal
In the Maktab Khana at Fatehpur Sikri
In the Tasvir Khana at Lahore
x: Urdu (Hindavi, Rekhta, Lashkari) grew out of military camps and bazaars, mixing Persian, Arabic, Turkic and local speech.

s: Who wrote the Deccani Urdu Tuti Nama (1639), based on the Sanskrit Shuka Saptati?
x: Ghavvasi wrote the Tuti Nama (1639) from the Sanskrit Shuka Saptati.

s: Which Qutb Shahi ruler, the first Urdu poet with a diwan, built the Charminar?
x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah was the first Urdu poet with a diwan and built the Charminar.

s: With whose reign is the Golden Age of Urdu associated?
x: The era of Abdullah Qutb Shah is described as the Golden Age of Urdu.

s: With which region was the Pahari school of painting (17th-19th centuries) associated?
x: Pahari painting flourished in the Sub-Himalayan region; the Bahmani link belongs to Deccani painting.

s: In the court of which dynasty did the Deccani school of painting begin?
x: Deccani painting began in the Bahmani court and continued in the successor states of the Bahmani kingdom.

s: Under which ruler did the Kangra sub-school of Pahari painting reach its peak?
x: Kangra flourished under Raja Sansar Chand.

s: Who was the major inspiration and patron of the Kishangarh School?
x: Raja Sawant Singh (Nagari Das) of Kishangarh was the inspiration and patron of the school. Nihalchand was his painter, while Farrukh Beg and Abul Hasan worked for the Mughals.

s: Who painted the Kishangarh painting 'Bani Thani'?
x: Bani Thani is by Nihal Chand, inspired by Sawant Singh's poem Bihari Jas Chandrika.

s: Who founded the Deccani school of painting at Golconda?
x: Mir Hashim founded Qutb Shahi Deccani painting at Golconda and was later invited to the Mughal court.

s: Which Later Mughal ruler released Shahu?
x: Bahadur Shah I, who reigned from 1707 to 1712, released Shahu.

s: Ghulam Qadir Rohilla blinded which Mughal emperor in 1788?
x: Shah Alam II was blinded by Ghulam Qadir; Ahmad Shah was blinded by Imad-ul-Mulk and Farrukh Siyar by the Sayyids.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Farrukhsiyar is correct?
o: He ruled from 1719 to 1748 and faced Nadir Shah's invasion.
He was a puppet of the Sayyid brothers and gave the English duty-free trade in Bengal.
He was the last Mughal emperor and ruled from 1837 to 1857.
He released Shahu immediately after Aurangzeb's death.
x: Farrukhsiyar ruled from 1713 to 1719, was controlled by the Sayyid brothers, executed Banda Singh Bahadur in 1716, and granted the English duty-free trade in Bengal.

s: Which event took place during the reign of Alamgir II?
x: The Battle of Plassey (1757) and repeated invasions by Ahmad Shah Abdali occurred during Alamgir II's reign.

s: Under whose protection did Shah Alam II return to Delhi in 1771-72?
x: After living at Allahabad under Company protection, Shah Alam II returned to Delhi under Mahadji Scindia's protection.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bahadur Shah II — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
Shah Alam II — Blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla
Akbar II — Gave Ram Mohan Roy the title ‘Raja’
Muhammad Shah — Exiled to Rangoon after 1857
x: Muhammad Shah was not exiled to Rangoon. Bahadur Shah II was exiled to Rangoon after the Revolt of 1857; Shah Alam II was blinded by Ghulam Qadir Rohilla.

s: During whose reign were Punjab and Multan ceded to Ahmad Shah Abdali?
x: Punjab and Multan were ceded to Ahmad Shah Abdali in the reign of Alamgir II (1754-1759), during Abdali's repeated invasions.

s: Which Later Mughal was called 'Lampat' (the profligate)?
x: Jahandar Shah, who was under his mistress Lal Kunwar, was called 'Lampat'.

s: By what name was Bahadur Shah I called?
x: Bahadur Shah I was Shah-i-Bekhabar; Muhammad Shah was Rangeela, Jahandar Shah Lampat and Aurangzeb Zinda Pir.

s: Who blinded and deposed the Mughal emperor Ahmad Shah in 1754?
x: Imad-ul-Mulk blinded and deposed Ahmad Shah in 1754; Ghulam Qadir blinded Shah Alam II in 1788.

s: During whose reign was Banda Singh Bahadur executed in 1716?
x: Farrukhsiyar (1713-1719) executed Banda Singh Bahadur in 1716.

s: Which Later Mughal is NOT correctly matched with his reign?
x: Ahmad Shah ruled 1748-1754, not to 1757, which would overlap Alamgir II.

s: Which of the following about the order of accession of the Later Mughals is NOT correct?
o: Bahadur Shah I came before Jahandar Shah
Shah Alam II came before Jahandar Shah
Farrukhsiyar came before Shah Alam II
x: The order is Bahadur Shah I, Jahandar Shah, Farrukhsiyar and Shah Alam II, so Shah Alam II came after Jahandar Shah.

s: After the revolt of 1857, which Mughal emperor was exiled to Rangoon?
x: Bahadur Shah II (Zafar) was exiled to Rangoon and died in 1862; Muhammad Shah was not exiled.

s: Who was the wazir of the Mughal emperor Jahandar Shah?
x: Jahandar Shah's wazir was Zulfiqar Khan; the Sayyids dominated Farrukhsiyar.

s: In which year did the English capture Delhi, during the reign of Shah Alam II?
x: The English captured Delhi in 1803, in Shah Alam II's reign.

s: Who was the first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company?
x: Shah Alam II became the Company's first Mughal pensioner.

s: Who became Mughal emperor immediately after Aurangzeb in 1707?
x: Bahadur Shah I (1707-1712) was the first emperor after Aurangzeb, followed by Jahandar Shah.

s: Who was the immediate predecessor of Farrukhsiyar on the Mughal throne?
x: Farrukhsiyar, with the Sayyid Brothers, killed Jahandar Shah (1712-1713) and took the throne in 1713.

s:
Arrange the following Later Mughals in chronological order:
1. Muhammad Shah
2. Bahadur Shah I
3. Shah Alam II
4. Farrukhsiyar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Bahadur Shah I (1707) came first, then Farrukhsiyar (1713), Muhammad Shah (1719) and Shah Alam II (1759).

s: Which Mughal emperor granted the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the British by the Treaty of Allahabad?
x: After Buxar, Shah Alam II gave the Diwani to the Company by the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).

s: Where was Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled after the revolt of 1857?
x: Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal, was exiled to Rangoon and died there in 1862.

s: Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah held which Mughal offices before establishing the Asaf Jahi state?
o: Subedar of the Deccan and Wazir
Nawab of Carnatic and Mir Bakshi
Subedar of Bengal and Diwan of Awadh
Diwan of Bengal and Subedar of Gujarat
x: Nizam-ul-Mulk was Subedar of the Deccan and also served as Wazir in the Mughal administration.

s: Which one of the following statements about the first Nizam is correct?
o: He accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
He kept the Marathas out of Hyderabad during his lifetime.
He was defeated at Shakar Kheda by Mubariz Khan.
x: The first Nizam kept the Marathas out during his lifetime. He died in 1748; the Subsidiary Alliance was accepted much later by Nizam Ali Khan.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Aurangzeb conferred the title Chin Qilich Khan, Farrukh Siyar conferred Nizam-ul-Mulk, and Muhammad Shah conferred Asaf Jah in 1725.

s: After helping overthrow the Sayyid brothers, whom did Nizam-ul-Mulk appoint as Diwan?
x: Nizam-ul-Mulk helped overthrow the Sayyids and appointed Puran Chand as Diwan.

s: Through which operation was Hyderabad State integrated into the Indian Union in 1948?
x: Operation Polo integrated Hyderabad in 1948; Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last Nizam.

s: Where did Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan, founder of the Asaf Jahi state, defeat Mubariz Khan?
x: He defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda; the state was founded in 1724.

s: Who conferred the title 'Nizam-ul-Mulk' on Mir Qamar-ud-din?
x: Farrukhsiyar gave the title Nizam-ul-Mulk; Aurangzeb gave Chin Qilich Khan.

s: Why are Nasir Jung, Muzaffar Jung and Salabat Jung not counted among the seven Nizams?
o: Did not receive the title Asaf Jah
x: The three did not receive the title Asaf Jah and so are not counted among the official seven Nizams.

s: Who conferred the title 'Asaf Jah' on the founder of Hyderabad in 1725?
x: Asaf Jah came from Muhammad Shah (1725); Chin Qilich Khan from Aurangzeb and Nizam-ul-Mulk from Farrukhsiyar.

s: Who was the seventh and last Nizam of Hyderabad?
x: Mir Osman Ali Khan (1911-1948) was the seventh and last Nizam; he founded Osmania University.

s: Which Nizam of Hyderabad signed Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance in 1798?
x: Nizam Ali Khan (Asaf Jah II, 1762-1803) accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798, not the first Nizam.

s: In which year did Nizam-ul-Mulk become virtually independent after defeating Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda?
x: The victory at Shakar Kheda in 1724 made Nizam-ul-Mulk virtually independent; 1724 is the founding year of Hyderabad state.

s: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan Siddiqi was the founder of which dynasty?
x: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan Siddiqi (Nizam-ul-Mulk) founded the Asaf Jahi dynasty and was the first Nizam of Hyderabad.

s: Which Nizam of Hyderabad founded the Osmania University?
x: Mir Osman Ali Khan, the seventh and last Nizam, founded Osmania University.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Saadat Khan was also known as Burhan-ul-Mulk.
Nizam-ul-Mulk was also known as Asaf-Jah.
Saadat Khan was also known as Sarvalokeshvara.
Chin Qilich Khan was also known as Nizam-ul-Mulk.
x: Option C is incorrect: Saadat Khan of Awadh was titled Burhan-ul-Mulk; Sarvalokeshvara was the title of the Kushana king Vima Kadphises. Chin Qilich Khan as Nizam-ul-Mulk and Asaf Jah is right.

s: How was Safdar Jung, who succeeded Saadat Khan as Nawab of Awadh, related to Saadat Khan?
x: Safdar Jung was Saadat Khan's nephew and son-in-law and also became Wazir.

s: Murshid Quli Khan held which offices in Bengal?
x: Murshid Quli Khan first served as Diwan and later became Nazim of Bengal. He ruled Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

s: Who founded the Carnatic state of Arcot?
x: Arcot was founded by Saadatullah Khan; Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk founded Awadh.

s: The Iranis are credited with establishing which successor state?
x: The Iranis established Oudh, while the Turanis established Hyderabad.

s: Who was the Afghan chief who carved out Rohilkhand during Nadir Shah's invasion?
x: Ali Muhammad Khan founded Rohilkhand; Muhammad Khan Bangash founded Farrukhabad.

s: Which founder of a successor state started revenue farming in Bengal?
x: Murshid Quli Khan, Diwan and then Nazim of Bengal, started revenue farming.

s: Which group of nobles is credited with establishing Hyderabad?
x: Turanis established Hyderabad; Iranis established Oudh.

s: Who founded the Afghan state of Farrukhabad?
x: Muhammad Khan Bangash, an Afghan adventurer, founded Farrukhabad.

s: Which Jat ruler of Bharatpur was called the 'Plato of the Jat tribe'?
x: Suraj Mal (1755-63) of Bharatpur was called the Plato of the Jat tribe.

s: Which fort was built by the Jat ruler Suraj Mal?
x: Suraj Mal built the Lohagarh fort at Bharatpur.

s: Whom did Saadatullah Khan name as his successor, making the Carnatic nawabship hereditary?
x: Saadatullah Khan, founder of Arcot, named his nephew Dost Ali successor without the Nizam's approval.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mughal successor states:
1. Murshid Quli Khan founded the Bengal state.
2. Saadatullah Khan founded the Awadh state.
3. Nizam-ul-Mulk became autonomous after defeating Mubariz Khan at Shakarkheda.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Murshid Quli Khan founded Bengal and Nizam-ul-Mulk won at Shakarkheda in 1724; Awadh was founded by Saadat Khan, while Saadatullah Khan founded Arcot.

s: Who founded the Mughal successor state of Awadh?
x: Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk, governor from 1722, founded Awadh; Saadatullah Khan founded Arcot.

s: Who fought the battles of Tarain and Chandawar?
x: Muhammad Ghori fought at Tarain and Chandawar; Mahmud Ghazni made 17 raids.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Alexander defeated Porus at the Jhelum.
Skandagupta defeated the first Huna invasion.
Muhammad bin Qasim conquered North India.
The Sakas were later defeated by Chandragupta II.
x: Option C is incorrect: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 CE, not North India. Alexander beat Porus at the Jhelum, Skandagupta repelled the Hunas and Chandragupta II defeated the Sakas.

s: Which of the following pairs (Invader – Victory) is NOT correctly matched?
x: Babur, not Timur, won at Panipat in 1526; Timur sacked Delhi in 1398.

s: In which year was the First Battle of Tarain fought?
x: First Tarain was fought in 1191; Timur came in 1398, Panipat I was 1526 and Karnal 1739.

s: In which year did Nadir Shah defeat the Mughals at the Battle of Karnal?
x: In 1739 Nadir Shah won at Karnal and then sacked Delhi.

s: In which year did Muhammad Ghori first invade India?
x: Muhammad Ghori's first invasion was in 1175.

s: From which year did Ahmad Shah Abdali's raids into India begin?
x: Abdali's raids began in 1748 and culminated at Panipat in 1761; Nadir Shah raided in 1739.

s: Along with Shah Jahan's Peacock Throne, which diamond did Nadir Shah carry away?
x: In 1739 Nadir Shah sacked Delhi and carried away the Koh-i-Noor and the Peacock Throne.

s:
Arrange the following invaders or groups in chronological order:
A. Hunas
B. Arabs under Muhammad bin Qasim
C. Kushanas
D. Greeks under Alexander
x: Alexander came in 326 BCE, the Kushanas in the 1st century CE, the Hunas in the 5th century CE and Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 CE, giving D, C, A, B.

s: Who defeated the Huna ruler Mihirakula?
x: Mihirakula was defeated by Yashodharman.

s: At the battle of which river did Alexander defeat Porus?
x: Alexander defeated Porus at the Hydaspes.

s: Who was the first ruler stated to have invaded parts of India?
x: Darius I of Persia (Achaemenid) was the first foreign ruler to invade parts of north-west India, around 518 BCE, before Alexander.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Sakas ruled western India. Darius I invaded NW India, Alexander fought Porus and the Hunas attacked the Gupta Empire.

s: Who was the contemporary historian of Nadir Shah's invasion?
x: Anand Ram Mukhlis was Nadir Shah's contemporary historian.

s: Whom did Ahmad Shah Abdali place on the Mughal throne in 1757?
x: In 1757 Abdali made Alamgir II emperor and Imad-ul-Mulk Prime Minister.

s: Who led the Persian invasion of north-western India?
x: Darius I led the Persian invasion; Alexander led the Greek one.

s: Which region did Muhammad bin Qasim, the first successful Muslim invader (712 CE), conquer?
x: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh, not North India, and killed Dahir.

s: How many times did Mahmud of Ghazni raid India?
x: Mahmud of Ghazni made 17 raids into India.

s: In which year did Timur sack Delhi?
x: Timur sacked Delhi in 1398, under Nasiruddin Mahmud of the Tughlaqs.

s: During the reign of which Delhi Sultan did Genghis Khan reach the Indus?
x: Genghis Khan reached the Indus in the 13th century under Iltutmish.

s: Ahmad Shah Abdali had earlier been a general of whom?
x: Abdali was Nadir Shah's general and took the Afghan throne in 1747.

s: On which date did Ahmad Shah Abdali win the Third Battle of Panipat?
x: Abdali defeated the Marathas at Third Panipat on 14 January 1761; Karnal (24 February 1739) was Nadir Shah's victory.

s: Which of the following about Nadir Shah is NOT correct?
o: He was the Afsharid ruler of Iran
He defeated Muhammad Shah at Karnal in 1739
He carried away Shah Jahan's Peacock Throne
He won the Third Battle of Panipat
x: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was won by Ahmad Shah Abdali, a commander of Nadir Shah.

s: For about how many years did Aurangzeb campaign in the Deccan at the end of his reign, draining the treasury?
x: Aurangzeb spent roughly the last twenty-seven years of his reign campaigning in the Deccan against the Marathas, which drained the Mughal treasury.

s: Which groups did Aurangzeb's reimposition of jizya in 1679 particularly alienate?
x: The religious policy, including the reimposition of jizya in 1679, alienated important groups such as the Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs.

s: By whom was the power vacuum left by the decline of the Mughal Empire successively filled?
o: Regional states, the Marathas and finally the East India Company
The Rajputs, the Sikhs and the Portuguese
The Mughals, the Marathas and the Ottoman Empire
The Sayyids, the Afghans and the French alone
x: The decline opened space for regional successor states, the Marathas and ultimately the East India Company.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a major cause of the decline of the Mughal Empire?
o: The invasions of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali
The long Deccan wars and the resulting drain on the treasury
The strengthening of central authority by independent nobles
x: Independent nobles weakened, rather than strengthened, central authority. The Deccan wars, Maratha rise and invasions were among the major causes of decline.

s: At its greatest extent under Aurangzeb, how far did the Mughal Empire extend?
o: Kashmir to Jinji and the Hindukush to Chittagong
Kabul to Bijapur and Sindh to Assam
Punjab to Madurai and the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal
Delhi to the Narmada and Gujarat to Bengal
x: Under Aurangzeb the empire reached from Kashmir to Jinji and from the Hindukush to Chittagong.

s:
Assertion (A): The foundations of the Mughal Empire were weakened after Aurangzeb.
Reason (R): Aurangzeb's long Deccan wars drained the treasury.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: The prolonged Deccan wars drained the treasury and weakened the empire's foundations, so R explains A.

s: How does the revisionist interpretation view the eighteenth century in India?
o: Exclusive European control over the peasant surplus
Regional growth, with successor states controlling economic and law-and-order systems
Uninterrupted Mughal centralisation under weak successors
x: The revisionist view treats the eighteenth century as a period of regional growth. The new states managed their own economic and law-and-order systems and controlled peasant surplus.

s: To what did François Bernier mainly trace Mughal decline?
o: The absence of private property in land
A shortage of nobles in imperial service
x: Bernier held that the absence of private property in land removed the incentive to improve it and led towards ruin.

s: Who wrote both History of Aurangzeb and Fall of the Mughal Empire?
x: Jadunath Sarkar authored both History of Aurangzeb and Fall of the Mughal Empire.

s: With which historian is the agrarian-crisis interpretation of Mughal decline, stressing over-exploitation of peasants and the resulting revolts, associated?
x: Irfan Habib explained the decline through an agrarian crisis in The Agrarian System of Mughal India (1963), arguing that over-exploitation of peasants provoked revolts.

s: To what did M. Athar Ali mainly attribute the worsening of the jagir shortage?
o: The transfer of all jagirs to European companies
The enlargement of the nobility through the inclusion of Deccanis and Marathas
The abolition of the mansabdari system by Farrukh Siyar
The decline of agriculture caused by Nadir Shah's raid
x: Athar Ali argued that the enlarged nobility, including Deccanis and Marathas, intensified the shortage of jagirs.

s: With which historian is the jagirdari-crisis explanation of Mughal decline (too few jagirs for too many nobles) associated?
x: Satish Chandra stressed the jagirdari crisis; Irfan Habib stressed the agrarian crisis.

s: Who wrote 'The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb'?
x: M. Athar Ali wrote The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb.

s: How did W.H. Moreland, author of 'From Akbar to Aurangzeb', mainly explain Mughal decline?
o: Absence of private property in land
An enlarged nobility of Deccanis and Marathas
x: Moreland stressed economic exploitation and stagnation; Bernier stressed the lack of private property in land.

s: Which post did Husain Ali Khan, one of the Sayyid brothers, hold?
x: Husain Ali Khan was Mir Bakhshi and Abdullah Khan the Wazir; they dominated Mughal politics from 1713 to 1720.

s: Which post did Abdullah Khan, one of the Sayyid brothers, hold?
x: Abdullah Khan was the Wazir and Husain Ali Khan the Mir Bakhshi.

s: During whose reign were the Sayyid brothers eliminated with Nizam-ul-Mulk's help?
x: Muhammad Shah removed the Sayyids with Nizam-ul-Mulk's help; Husain Ali was killed in 1720.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Sayyid brothers:
1. They were king-makers from 1713 to 1720.
2. Husain Ali Khan was killed in 1720.
3. Saadat Khan sided with them against Muhammad Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Sayyids were king-makers in 1713-1720 and Husain Ali was killed in 1720; Saadat Khan joined the plot against them, siding with Muhammad Shah.

s: Why is the Farman of 1717 issued by Farrukh Siyar significant?
o: Granted chauth and sardeshmukhi to Shahu's agent
Exempted the English Company from customs duties in Bengal
Granted the Company Diwani rights in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
Transferred Kora and Allahabad to the Company
x: The Farman of 1717 exempted the Company from customs duties in Bengal and was called the Company's Magna Carta.

s: What did the Mughal grant of 1719, issued through the Sayyids, give to Balaji Vishwanath as Shahu's agent?
o: Diwani rights in Bengal and Bihar
Kora and Allahabad with an annual payment
Chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas
x: The 1719 grant recognised Shahu's claim to chauth and sardeshmukhi from the six Deccan subas through his agent Balaji Vishwanath.

s: Which of the following about the Mughal grants of 1719 to the Marathas is NOT correct?
o: They gave chauth and sardeshmukhi of eight Deccan subas
They gave chauth and sardeshmukhi of six Deccan subas
x: The 1719 grants covered the six Deccan subas, not eight; they also recognised Shahu and confirmed the Swarajya lands.

s: With whose help were the Sayyid brothers, Abdullah Khan and Husain Ali Khan, overthrown?
x: They were overthrown with the help of Nizam-ul-Mulk, not Murshid Quli Khan.

s: What was the role of the Nyayadhish in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan?
o: Keeper of intelligence and the king's diary
x: The Nyayadhish was the chief justice; the Amatya handled finance, the Panditrao religion and the Mantri intelligence.

s: To whom did every minister of Shivaji's Ashtapradhan report directly?
x: Each minister reported to the Chhatrapati; posts were not hereditary and ministers could be transferred or dismissed.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Peshwa post is NOT correct?
o: The post was hereditary and supreme from the beginning of Shivaji's Ashtapradhan.
The post was associated with general administration.
The post became hereditary and supreme under the later Peshwas.
Initially, the Peshwa was the Prime Minister of Shivaji.
x: The Peshwa post became hereditary and supreme only later, under the Peshwas; it was not hereditary and supreme from the beginning of Shivaji's administration.

s: Which of the following Ashtapradhan titles is wrongly matched with its portfolio?
o: Waqia-navis – Intelligence and the king's diary
x: The Dabir (Sumant) handled foreign affairs; treasury and revenue belonged to the Amatya.

s: What did the Mantri (Waqia-navis) look after in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan?
x: The Mantri handled intelligence, the king's diary and the household; the Sumant handled foreign affairs.

s: Of which department was the Amatya (Majumdar) in charge in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan?
x: The Amatya (Majumdar) handled finance: treasury, accounts and revenue.

s: What did the Sachiv (Surnis) handle in Shivaji's Ashtapradhan?
x: The Sachiv dealt with royal correspondence and records; the Mantri dealt with intelligence.

s: Which two Ashtapradhan ministers were exempt from leading military campaigns?
x: All ministers except the Panditrao and the Nyayadhish had to lead military campaigns.

s: Which minister of Shivaji's Ashtapradhan was in charge of religious affairs and charitable grants?
x: The Panditrao (Danadhyaksha) looked after religious affairs and charitable grants.

s: Shivaji's Ashtapradhan was ____, whereas the Mughal wazir system was hierarchical.
x: The Ashtapradhan was advisory and the Mughal wazir system hierarchical; Shivaji also paid in cash rather than jagirs.

s:
Assertion (A): Shivaji assumed the title Chhatrapati in 1674.
Reason (R): Gaga Bhatta, also known as Vishweshwar, performed Shivaji's formal coronation.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: at the 1674 coronation at Raigarh, performed by Gaga Bhatta (Vishweshwar) of Varanasi, Shivaji was crowned and took the title Chhatrapati.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the rise of the Marathas?
o: The Sahyadri hills and hill forts favoured guerrilla warfare.
Aurangzeb's Deccan campaign strengthened Mughal finances.
Bhakti saints promoted spiritual and regional unity.
Marathas had served in the armies and revenue offices of the Deccan Sultanates.
x: Aurangzeb's 27-year Deccan campaign drained the Mughal treasury rather than strengthening it.

s: Before Shivaji, in the service of which states did the Marathas gain military and revenue experience?
x: Marathas, Shahaji among them, served in the armies and revenue posts of Bijapur and Ahmadnagar.

s: Which hill range had forts that suited Maratha guerrilla war?
x: The Sahyadri hills and their hill forts suited guerrilla warfare.

s: With which Mughal weakness was the opportunity for the Maratha rise associated?
o: the Mughal conquest of Golconda in 1672 and the Treaty of Purandar
Aurangzeb’s short Deccan campaign and stable succession after 1707
the consolidation of Mughal finances through the Deccan revenues
Aurangzeb’s 27-year Deccan campaign and the succession war after 1707
x: The prolonged Deccan campaign drained the treasury, while the succession war after 1707 created a political vacuum.

s: In which year did Shivaji capture Torna from Bijapur?
x: Shivaji seized Torna from Bijapur in 1646, and it was his first fort.

s: What was the role of Dadaji Kondadev in Shivaji's early career?
o: guardian of the Pune jagir and Shivaji’s tutor
commander of the Bijapur army at Panhala
Mughal envoy who negotiated the Treaty of Purandar
x: Dadaji Kondadev served as guardian of the Pune jagir and acted as Shivaji’s tutor.

s: Which one of the following statements about Shivaji’s early life is correct?
o: He was born at Torna in 1630 to Dadaji Kondadev and Jijabai.
He was born at Shivneri in 1630 to Shahaji Bhonsle and Jijabai.
He was born at Raigad in 1646 to Shahaji and Tarabai.
He was born at Pratapgad in 1656 to Shahaji and Soyarabai.
x: Shivaji was born in 1630 at Shivneri fort to Shahaji Bhonsle, a Maratha general, and Jijabai.

s: Which post did Akkanna hold in Golconda?
x: Akkanna was Sar Lashkar and Madanna the Mir Jumla of Golconda.

s: Which work was written by Samarth Ramdas, traditionally named as Shivaji's guru?
x: Samarth Ramdas wrote the Dasbodh; Shivaji's guardian was Dadaji Kondadev.

s: From whom did Shivaji take Raigad in 1656?
x: Raigad was taken from the Mores of Javli in 1656 and later became the capital and coronation site.

s: Besides Samarth Ramdas, which saint contemporary of Shivaji shaped the spiritual base of the Maratha rise?
x: Tukaram and Ramdas gave the Marathas spiritual and regional unity.

s:
Consider the following statements about Shivaji's early life:
1. He was born at Shivneri fort.
2. Dadaji Kondadev was the keeper of the Pune jagir and his tutor.
3. Torna, his first fort, was taken from the Mughals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Shivaji was born at Shivneri and tutored by Dadaji Kondadev; Torna (1646) was taken from Bijapur, not the Mughals.

s: Who accompanied Shivaji during his escape from house arrest at Agra in 1666?
x: Shivaji escaped together with Sambhaji, hidden in baskets of sweets and fruit.

s: In which year did Shivaji's coronation at Raigad take place?
x: Coronation 1674; second Surat raid 1670; treaty with Tana Shah 1677; death 1680.

s: At the foot of which fort did Shivaji kill the Bijapur general Afzal Khan in 1659?
x: Shivaji killed Afzal Khan with a wagh nakh at the foot of Pratapgad.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the event associated with Shivaji?
o: 1670 — Defeat of Afzal Khan at Pratapgad
1663 — Night raid on Shaista Khan at Pune
x: In 1663, Shivaji conducted a night raid on Shaista Khan at Pune, during which Khan lost his fingers and retreated.

s: Under the treaty between Shivaji and Abul Hasan Tana Shah, Golconda agreed to provide money for the southern conquests and
o: send Sambhaji to the Mughal court
x: The agreement provided financial support from Golconda for the southern conquests, with the spoils to be shared.

s: In his southern campaign, Shivaji took Gingee, Ballari and which other place?
x: Shivaji took Gingee, Vellore and Ballari and refused to share the spoils.

s: Where was Shivaji crowned 'Chhatrapati' in 1674?
x: Shivaji's coronation as Chhatrapati took place at Raigad in 1674. Agra is where he was placed under house arrest in 1666, Jinji was Rajaram's base, and Kolhapur was the seat of Tarabai's later line.

s: Shivaji sacked the Mughal port of Surat in 1664. In which year did he sack it again?
x: Shivaji sacked Surat twice, in 1664 and 1670, taking nearly one crore rupees.

s: Afzal Khan, killed by Shivaji in 1659, was a general of which state?
x: Afzal Khan was a Bijapur general; Shaista Khan was a Mughal noble.

s: How many forts did Shivaji cede under the Treaty of Purandar (1665)?
x: At Purandar Shivaji ceded 23 of 35 forts and sent Sambhaji to the Mughal court.

s: Which post was held by Madanna, who arranged Golconda's 1677 treaty with Shivaji?
x: Madanna was the Mir Jumla of Golconda; his brother Akkanna was the Sar Lashkar.

s: From whom did Shivaji take Vellore in the Karnataka campaign of 1677?
x: Shivaji took Vellore from his step-brother Venkoji (Ekoji) in 1677.

s:
Arrange the following events of Shivaji's career in chronological order:
1. Treaty of Purandar
2. Killing of Afzal Khan
3. Night raid on Shaista Khan
4. Escape from Agra
x: Afzal Khan was killed in 1659, Shaista Khan raided in 1663, Purandar was signed in 1665 and the Agra escape was in 1666.

s: Whom did the Marathas defeat in open battle at Salher in 1672?
x: At Salher in 1672 the Marathas defeated the Mughals in open battle.

s: On which Mughal noble did Shivaji make a night raid at Pune in 1663?
x: In 1663 Shivaji raided Shaista Khan, Aurangzeb's maternal uncle, at Pune; the Khan lost his fingers and retreated.

s: Which Mughal general, along with Raja Jai Singh, besieged Shivaji before the Treaty of Purandar?
x: The Mughal force under Raja Jai Singh, with Diler Khan, besieged Purandar and forced the treaty of 1665.

s: Under the Treaty of Purandar, which son of Shivaji was sent to the Mughal court?
x: By the Treaty of Purandar (1665) Shivaji ceded 23 forts and sent his son Sambhaji to the Mughal court.

s: How was Shaista Khan, on whom Shivaji made a night raid at Pune, related to Aurangzeb?
x: Shaista Khan was Aurangzeb's maternal uncle.

s: In which year did Shivaji die?
x: Shivaji died in 1680; Sambhaji then ruled till 1689.

s: Who officiated at Shivaji's coronation with Vedic rites?
x: Gaga Bhatt, a learned Brahmin from Banaras (Varanasi), officiated at the coronation with Vedic rites.

s: Which title did Shivaji adopt at his coronation?
x: The coronation title was 'Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati'; he was also styled Haindava Dharmoddharak, not Hindavi Sultan.

s: What was the era started by Shivaji to assert sovereignty against the Mughals and the Sultanates called?
x: Shivaji began the Rajabhisheka Shaka after his coronation to assert sovereign status.

s: Besides 'Shri Raja Shiva Chhatrapati', which title did Shivaji assume at his coronation?
x: Shivaji also took the title Haindava Dharmoddharak, not 'Hindavi Sultan'.

s:
Consider the following statements about Shivaji's coronation:
1. It took place at Raigad in 1674.
2. Shivaji took the title 'Hindavi Sultan'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: He was crowned at Raigad in 1674 and took the title Haindava Dharmoddharak, not Hindavi Sultan.

s:
Arrange the following rulers in chronological order of their succession in the Maratha polity:
A. Shahu
B. Sambhaji
C. Tarabai
D. Rajaram
x: The sequence was Sambhaji, Rajaram, Tarabai as regent for Shivaji II, and Shahu.

s: From where did Rajaram, who created the post of Pratinidhi, direct Maratha resistance against Aurangzeb?
x: Rajaram directed resistance from Gingee (Jinji) and drew Aurangzeb south.

s: Under which treaty was Tarabai's line later settled at Kolhapur?
x: Tarabai's line was settled at Kolhapur under the Treaty of Warna.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Shahu is correct?
o: He was released by Bahadur Shah I, defeated Tarabai's forces at Khed, and ruled from Satara.
He moved to Gingee and created the post of Pratinidhi.
He was captured and executed by Aurangzeb in 1689.
He led the Marathas at Aurangzeb's death as Rajaram's widow.
x: Shahu was released by Bahadur Shah I in 1707, defeated Tarabai at Khed, and ruled from Satara.

s: Who released Shahu from Mughal custody in 1707?
x: Bahadur Shah I released Shahu in 1707, not Aurangzeb.

s: At which battle did Shahu defeat Tarabai in 1707?
x: Shahu beat Tarabai at Khed in 1707 and ruled from Satara.

s: Who captured and executed Sambhaji, Shivaji's successor, in 1689?
x: Aurangzeb executed Sambhaji in 1689, after which the conflict became a people's war.

s:
Consider the following statements about Shivaji's successors:
1. Rajaram created the post of Pratinidhi.
2. Tarabai's line was settled at Kolhapur by the Treaty of Warna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rajaram created the Pratinidhi post and moved to Gingee; Tarabai's line was settled at Kolhapur by the Treaty of Warna (1731).

s: At its peak, the Maratha Empire extended from Attock to which place?
x: The Maratha Empire ran from Attock to Cuttack and from the Gulf of Khambhat to beyond the Kaveri.

s: Who appointed Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa in 1713?
x: Shahu appointed Balaji Vishwanath (Peshwa 1713-20); real power then shifted from the Chhatrapati to the Peshwa.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Baji Rao I – Major expansion in North India
Shivaji – Major expansion in North India
x: Baji Rao I led the Maratha expansion into North India; Shivaji founded the state with the Ashtapradhan, Sambhaji resisted the Mughals and Balaji Vishwanath consolidated Peshwa power.

s: Under which Peshwa did major Maratha expansion in North India take place?
x: Baji Rao I (1720-1740) led major expansion in North India.

s: The combined effect of chauth and sardeshmukhi was to
o: finance military expansion and establish political hegemony without the cost of direct governance
confine Maratha authority to the fort of Raigad
replace the Ashtapradhan with a hereditary Mughal bureaucracy
end Maratha military expansion by restricting revenue collection
x: Together, the levies financed military expansion and extended political hegemony without requiring the Marathas to administer every territory directly.

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes chauth from sardeshmukhi?
o: Chauth: 25% protection levy; sardeshmukhi: additional 10% hereditary claim
Chauth: 25% hereditary claim; sardeshmukhi: 10% protection levy
Chauth: 10% hereditary claim; sardeshmukhi: 25% protection levy
Chauth: 10% protection levy; sardeshmukhi: additional 25% hereditary claim
x: Chauth was generally one-fourth of land revenue as protection money; sardeshmukhi was an additional 10 per cent claimed as the king's hereditary right as Sardeshmukh.

s: From which areas was chauth mainly collected?
o: territories under direct Maratha administration only
the personal estates of the Ashtapradhan ministers
x: Chauth was levied on territories outside direct Maratha rule, including Mughal and Deccan Sultanate territories.

s: In which year did the burden of paying chauth after the 1795 war push the Nizam into the British Subsidiary Alliance?
x: After the 1795 war the Nizam paid chauth to the Marathas, which contributed to his joining the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.

s: Where did the Nizam concede Maratha claims to chauth and sardeshmukhi?
x: The Nizam conceded chauth and sardeshmukhi at Palkhed; the Mughals had conceded them in 1719.

s: What were the provinces outside direct Maratha rule, from which chauth was collected, called?
x: Chauth came from lands outside direct Maratha rule, called Mughalai; Swarajya was the Maratha home territory.

s: Which of the following about chauth is NOT correct?
o: It was one-fourth of the land revenue
It was a kind of protection money
It was collected from lands outside direct Maratha rule
It was claimed as the hereditary right of the Sardeshmukh
x: The hereditary right of the Sardeshmukh was the basis of sardeshmukhi, not chauth.

s: Chauth was a levy of what share of the land revenue?
x: Chauth was 25% of land revenue; sardeshmukhi was an additional 10%.

s: What was the rate of sardeshmukhi, an additional levy?
x: Sardeshmukhi was an extra 10%, claimed as the king's hereditary right as Sardeshmukh of the Deccan.

s: Shivaji's revenue settlement, in which the state dealt directly with the cultivator, was of which type?
x: Shivaji dealt directly with cultivators in a ryotwari-type settlement and paid officials in cash.

s: What were the service land grants that Shivaji abolished, but which returned under Shahu and the Peshwas, called?
x: Shivaji abolished jagirs and paid in cash; saranjam grants returned under Shahu and the Peshwas.

s: In Maratha revenue terminology, what did 'Bagayat' denote?
x: Bagayat was irrigated land, Jirayat dry land and Kathi a measuring rod.

s: Under Shivaji's administration, which pair (unit – official) is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Pargana had the Deshmukh and Deshpande; the Patil and Kulkarni served the Mauza (village).

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Shivaji's state?
o: Officials and forces paid in cash
x: Shivaji's state was centralised and non-hereditary, with officials paid in cash, not through hereditary jagirs.

s: In Shivaji's revenue system, what was the 'kathi'?
x: The kathi was the measuring rod used in Annaji Datto's survey.

s: With whom is the land survey with the kathi under Shivaji associated?
x: Annaji Datto's survey used the kathi measuring rod.

s: In a mauza (village) under Shivaji, who was the Kulkarni?
x: The Patil was the village head and the Kulkarni the village accountant.

s:
Consider the following statements about Shivaji's revenue system:
1. Shivaji curbed the hereditary rights of the deshmukhs and deshpandes.
2. The big deshmukhs supported Shivaji's independent Maratha state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Shivaji curbed the watandar deshmukhs; the big deshmukhs opposed him because they wanted to stay under Bijapur.

s: With which replacement was the Rajvyavahar Kosh associated?
o: Persian official terms by Sanskrit terms
x: The Rajvyavahar Kosh replaced Persian official terminology with Sanskrit terminology.

s: Which one of the following correctly identifies Shivaji’s coins?
x: Shivaji issued the gold Hon and the copper Shivrai.

s: What does Ganimi Kava, associated with Shivaji's military tactics, refer to?
o: A treaty-based system of revenue collection
Guerrilla hit-and-run warfare in the Sahyadri terrain
A system of permanent fortified cantonments in the Deccan
A naval blockade of Mughal ports
x: Ganimi Kava was the guerrilla hit-and-run method used by Shivaji in the difficult Sahyadri terrain.

s: Under Shivaji, in which script were Marathi administrative records kept?
x: Marathi and Sanskrit were promoted over Persian, and the cursive Modi script was used for Marathi records.

s: Under Shivaji, of which metal was the 'Shivrai' coin made?
x: The Shivrai was a copper coin; the hon was gold and the Shivrai rupaya silver.

s: Which of the following groups contains only forts classified as Giri Durg?
x: Raigad, Pratapgad, Torna and Sinhagad are hill forts, or Giri Durg. Vishalgad is a land fort, while the others in the distractors include sea forts.

s: Which coast did Shivaji's sea forts such as Sindhudurg, Kolaba and Vijaydurg guard?
x: The sea forts guarded the Konkan coast; Shivaji is called the Father of the Indian Navy.

s: Each fort under Shivaji was placed under the charge of three officers of equal rank. Which set correctly identifies them?
x: The three officers were the Havaldar, Sabnis and Sarnobat. The Sabnis handled records, while the Havaldar and Sarnobat had garrison and military responsibilities.

s: What were Maratha cavalrymen who were given horses and equipment by the state called?
x: Bargirs were state-equipped cavalry; Shiledars maintained their own horses.

s: In Shivaji's fort administration, who was the Havaldar?
x: Each fort had a Havaldar (garrison commander), a Sabnis (records) and a Sarnaubat (military officer).

s: Which of the following was a Jal Durg (sea fort) of Shivaji?
x: Khanderi was a sea fort; Pratapgad and Sinhagad were hill forts and Vishalgad a land fort.

s: In Shivaji's army, the Shiledars were cavalrymen who:
o: Were given horses by the state
x: Shiledars kept their own horses, while Bargirs were given horses and equipment by the state.

s: Who is called the Father of the Indian Navy?
x: Shivaji built sea forts like Sindhudurg and Vijaydurg on the Konkan and is called the Father of the Indian Navy.

s: Under which name were the forts of the Marathas inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2025?
x: In 2025 UNESCO inscribed the 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India'.

s: In which year was the 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India' inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list?
x: It was inscribed in 2025.

s: What were the hill infantry soldiers of Shivaji called?
x: Mavali infantry were Shivaji's hill troops; Bargirs and Shiledars were cavalry.

s: Who was the Peshwa at the time of the Third Battle of Panipat?
x: Balaji Baji Rao, popularly known as Nana Saheb, was the Peshwa when the Third Battle of Panipat was fought.

s: Which Peshwa died soon after the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761?
x: Balaji Baji Rao died soon after the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761.

s: Which of the following was NOT a major cause of the Maratha defeat at Panipat?
o: Alienation of some regional powers through earlier plunder
Heavy baggage and the presence of non-combatants
Strong and sustained support from the Jats and Rajputs
Collapse of supplies and starvation in the camp
x: The Marathas did not receive strong support from the Jats and Rajputs; their absence or neutrality contributed to the defeat. Supply failure, heavy baggage and alienation of regional powers were among the causes.

s: Who commanded the Maratha artillery at the Third Battle of Panipat?
x: Ibrahim Khan Gardi led the Maratha artillery, while Sadashiv Rao Bhau was the overall commander.

s: Who invited Ahmad Shah Abdali to intervene, leading to the Third Battle of Panipat?
x: The Rohilla chief Najib-ud-Daula invited Abdali; Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh was an ally.

s: Which of the following groups consisted of important allies of Ahmad Shah Abdali at Panipat?
o: Suraj Mal and the Rajput chiefs
x: Abdali was supported by the Rohilla chief Najib-ud-Daula and Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh.

s: Who was the overall Maratha commander at the Third Battle of Panipat?
x: Sadashiv Rao Bhau was overall commander; Vishwas Rao was the Peshwa's son and Ibrahim Khan Gardi led the artillery.

s: Who was Abdali's son whom the Marathas drove out of Lahore in 1758?
x: The expulsion of Timur Shah from Lahore (1758) was Abdali's immediate motive for the Panipat campaign.

s: Kashiraj Pandit, who left an eyewitness account of the Third Battle of Panipat, was an official of whom?
x: Kashiraj Pandit, the eyewitness chronicler of Panipat (1761), was an official of Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh.

s: Which son of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao was killed in the Third Battle of Panipat?
x: Vishwas Rao, the Peshwa's son, and Sadashiv Rao Bhau were both killed at Panipat.

s: The Sangola agreement of 1750, which reduced the Chhatrapati to a nominal position, followed whose death?
x: The Sangola agreement followed Shahu's death in 1749 and consolidated the Peshwa's position.

s: In which year did Shahu make Balaji Vishwanath the Peshwa?
x: Shahu appointed Balaji Vishwanath Peshwa in November 1713; 1720 is when Baji Rao I succeeded him.

s: Which of the following best describes the achievement of Madhav Rao I after 1761?
o: He signed the Treaty of Bassein and became the last Peshwa.
He revived Maratha power after Panipat and defeated several regional opponents.
He founded Peshwa power and secured the 1719 Mughal grant.
He was removed by the Barabhai council immediately after his accession.
x: Madhav Rao I revived Maratha power after Panipat and defeated the Nizam, Mysore under Haidar Ali, Rohillas, Rajputs and Jats.

s: Through whom did the infant Peshwa Madhav Rao II rule?
x: Madhav Rao II, installed as an infant in 1774, ruled through Nana Phadnavis.
