s: Which Peshwa was popularly known as Nana Saheb?
x: Nana Saheb refers to Balaji Baji Rao, not Balaji Vishwanath.

s: Gujarat was brought under Maratha control during the tenure of which Peshwa?
x: Gujarat was taken under Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb, 1740-61), during whose tenure Maratha power reached its zenith (APPSC 2025). Balaji Vishwanath secured the 1719 grant; Baji Rao I won Malwa and Bundelkhand; Madhav Rao I revived power after Panipat.

s: The phrase "strike the trunk, the branches will fall" is associated with:
x: The phrase is Baji Rao I's, about striking at the Mughal centre; his ideology is expressed as Hindu Pad Padshahi.

s: By what name was Nana Phadnavis popularly known?
x: Nana Phadnavis was called the “Maratha Machiavelli” because of his political skill in managing the confederacy.

s: Which Peshwa won Malwa and Bundelkhand and raided Delhi in 1737?
x: Baji Rao I won Malwa and Bundelkhand and raided Delhi in 1737.

s: Who among the following is regarded as the most charismatic Maratha leader after Shivaji?
x: Baji Rao I is regarded as the most charismatic Maratha leader after Shivaji.

s: Baji Rao I organised the Maratha confederacy primarily in order to
o: keep the Maratha factions together and satisfy the older chiefs led by Senapati Dabhade
place the Maratha state under direct British protection
abolish the authority of Shahu immediately
transfer the capital from Poona to Nagpur
x: Baji Rao I built the confederacy to maintain unity among Maratha factions and to accommodate older chiefs led by Senapati Dabhade.

s: Who secured the 1719 Mughal grant of swarajya, chauth and sardeshmukhi of the Deccan?
x: Balaji Vishwanath obtained the 1719 Mughal grant through the Sayyid brothers.

s: What is the ideology of Baji Rao I known as?
x: Baji Rao I's ideology was Hindu Pad Padshahi. His slogan "strike the trunk, the branches will fall" meant striking at the Mughal centre.

s: By what other name was Balaji Baji Rao, Peshwa from 1740 to 1761, known?
x: Balaji Baji Rao was known as Nana Saheb; under him Maratha power reached its zenith, reaching Lahore and Peshawar.

x: Madhav Rao I (1761-72), Narayan Rao (1772-73), Madhav Rao II (1774-95) and Baji Rao II (1796-1818).

s: Who founded the Holkar house of the Maratha confederacy?
x: The Holkar house was founded by Malhar Rao Holkar; Ranoji Scindia founded the Scindia house.

s: Which of the following was the principal weakness of the Maratha confederacy?
o: Internal rivalries and conflicting regional interests
Direct Mughal control over all Maratha territories
x: The confederacy was weakened by rivalries among semi-independent chiefs and their tendency to put regional interests before common Maratha interests.

s: In the Maratha confederacy, what did 'saranjam' refer to?
o: A tax of one-fourth of land revenue
Land assignments to chiefs for military service
x: Saranjam grants were land assignments to chiefs for military service and formed the base of the confederacy.

s: The Peshwa Daftar records at Pune are written mostly in which script?
x: The Peshwa Daftar's diaries, orders and sanads are mostly in Modi script; Elphinstone preserved them after 1818.

s: Where was the seat of the Gaekwad house of the Maratha confederacy?
x: Gaekwad = Baroda; Bhonsle = Nagpur, Holkar = Indore and Scindia = Gwalior.

s: Who among the following was a leader of the Pindaris?
x: Chitu, Karim Khan and Wasil Muhammad were Pindari leaders; the Pindaris rode with the Maratha armies.

s: Which Governor-General crushed the Pindaris in 1817-18?
x: Lord Hastings (Marquess of Hastings) crushed the Pindaris in 1817-18, which also led to the Third Anglo-Maratha War.

s: Which was the seat of the Scindia (Shinde) house of the Maratha confederacy?
x: Scindia = Gwalior; Holkar = Indore; Gaekwad = Baroda; Bhonsle = Nagpur.

s: Who preserved the Peshwa Daftar records at Pune after 1818?
x: The Peshwa Daftar, mostly in Modi script, was preserved by Elphinstone after 1818.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Death of Peshwa Madhav Rao I – 1772
x: Madhav Rao I died in 1772, after which Peshwa control over the chiefs weakened further; Plassey was fought in 1757 and Wandiwash in 1760.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Raghunath Rao – Regent for the infant Madhav Rao II
Nana Phadnavis – Leader of the Barabhai council
Nana Phadnavis – Ally of Raghunath Rao
Madhav Rao II – Leader of the Barabhai council
x: Nana Phadnavis led the twelve-member Barabhai council, governed for the infant Madhav Rao II and opposed Raghunath Rao.

s: Which Maratha leader restored Shah Alam II to Delhi in 1771?
x: Mahadji Scindia recaptured Delhi and restored Shah Alam II in 1771, making the Marathas Mughal king-makers.

s: Nana Phadnavis led which twelve-member council of the Marathas?
x: Nana Phadnavis led the twelve-member Barabhai council and was regent for the infant Madhav Rao II.

s: Which Peshwa signed the Treaty of Bassein (1802)?
x: Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein; he was the last Peshwa.

s: How was Raghunath Rao (Raghoba) related to Peshwa Madhav Rao I?
x: Raghoba was Madhav Rao I's uncle, not his brother - a common trap.

s: Who was the last Peshwa?
x: Baji Rao II (1796-1818) was the last Peshwa; the Peshwaship was abolished in 1818.

s: The death of Nana Phadnavis in 1800 was followed by which development?
o: The Marathas immediately restored Mughal authority at Delhi
The Nizam recognised Maratha control over Malwa
Holkar and Scindia fought over the weak Peshwa, contributing to the Treaty of Bassein and the Second Anglo-Maratha War
Baji Rao I founded the Barabhai council
x: After Nana Phadnavis’s death, Holkar and Scindia competed for influence over the weak Peshwa in 1801–02. This contributed to the Treaty of Bassein and the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

s: After which battle did the Mungi-Shevgaon settlement between the Marathas and the Nizam come?
x: Mungi-Shevgaon was a peace settlement between the Marathas and the Nizam after Palkhed.

s: Whom did the Marathas defeat in the Battle of Kharda (1795)?
x: At Kharda in 1795 the Marathas defeated the Nizam of Hyderabad.

s: Between whom was the Treaty of Mungi-Shevgaon concluded?
o: the Marathas and the English East India Company
x: Mungi-Shevgaon was a treaty between the Marathas and the Nizam (APPSC 2025), signed after Baji Rao I defeated the Nizam at Palkhed (1728); it conceded chauth and sardeshmukhi of the Deccan. It did not involve the Mughals, the English or the Portuguese.

s: On whose neutrality did the Nizam, defeated by the Marathas in 1795, blame his defeat?
x: The Nizam blamed Sir John Shore's neutrality, which pushed him to the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.

s: After the Battle of Bhopal (Treaty of Doraha Sarai, 1738), which territory did the Nizam cede?
x: Defeated by Baji Rao I at Bhopal, the Nizam ceded Malwa under the Treaty of Doraha Sarai.

s: In which year was the Battle of Palkhed, in which Baji Rao I defeated Nizam-ul-Mulk, fought?
x: Palkhed (1728) led to the Treaty of Mungi-Shevgaon; 1760 was Udgir.

s: The First Anglo-Maratha War arose from a succession dispute after whose murder?
x: The war arose from the succession dispute after Narayan Rao's murder, when Raghunath Rao turned to the British.

s: Between whom was the Treaty of Salbai of 1782 concluded?
o: Lord Hastings and Baji Rao II
x: The Treaty of Salbai was concluded in 1782 between Warren Hastings and Mahadji Scindia. It restored the status quo and helped establish peace for twenty years.

x: After the British defeat at Talegaon, the Convention of Wadgaon forced them to give up their gains, but Warren Hastings rejected it.

s: Who was the Governor-General of India during the Third Anglo-Maratha War?
x: The Third Anglo-Maratha War was fought during the tenure of Lord Hastings, also known as the Marquess of Hastings.

s: Which of the following battles was NOT associated with the Third Anglo-Maratha War?
x: Khadki, Koregaon, Sitabuldi and Mahidpur were associated with the Third Anglo-Maratha War. Assaye belonged to the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
